key_insight: The paper shows that first-order optimization can still converge for convex problems with generalized [0;31m(L0, L1)[0m-smoothness when only an inexact normalized gradient is available from a comparison oracle.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical training and control pipelines where exact gradients are too costly or unreliable, especially in modern machine learning settings that violate classical Lipschitz-smooth assumptions.
method: Comparison-oracle version of Normalized Gradient Descent
Comparison-oracle Gradient Descent with Polyak stepsizes
Explicit error thresholds for convergence guarantees
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that corroborate the theoretical convergence results and error bounds.
watch_item: Performance depends on keeping the gradient-approximation error below derived upper bounds; exceeding these limits can break convergence guarantees.
paper_title: Normalized First-Order Methods for Convex (L0, L1)-Smooth Optimization with Inexact Gradients
